visualCharacteristics.purpose: Full-bleed photo hero with h1, subheading, address lookup form (from the "Check availability" link) and disclaimer
observed: Source hero: background photo, h1 'Fast, reliable satellite internet', subheading, address-lookup form (destination https://buy.viasat.com/en-US/r/), disclaimer text
Source hero + address-lookup: photo, h1 'Fast, reliable satellite internet plans for wherever you live', subheading, address field + Check availability

Source hero: photo (man on couch with laptop), h1 'Enhanced support with EasyCare', subheading, 'SAVE ON YOUR FIRST 3 MONTHS!*', two CTAs ('Not a customer? Shop internet plans' -> buy.viasat.com, 'Already a customer? Add EasyCare' -> my.viasat.com), disclaimer

contentPattern.structure: row 1: background image; row 2: h1, subheading paragraph, link "Check availability" -> https://buy.viasat.com/en-US/r/ (becomes the address form), other CTA links (stay buttons), disclaimer paragraph(s) after the last form/button

usage: Page-top hero on home, plans, easycare. Only a link whose text is "Check availability" and that points at buy.viasat.com/en-US/r/ becomes the address form (shared scripts/address-lookup.js); every other link stays a button. Paragraphs after the last form/button get .hero-lookup-disclaimer. Use the "left" option for the left-column layout (easycare hero).
reuseGuidance: Author the block name as "Hero Lookup" (class hero-lookup). "Hero (lookup)" would load the base hero with a "lookup" option instead.
